measurement.order: before-1, after-1, before-2, after-2, before-3, after-3
measurement.server: local HTTP; no-store; no transfer compression

checks: Cold home contains static content and fetches no gallery, game code or audio
First section visits load features once and preserve game, gallery and music state
Back, forward and repeated navigation preserve one history entry per destination
Manual scrolling updates a single active navigation link without growing history
Reduced motion, sticky-header offsets and phone/tablet/desktop layouts remain usable
Direct deep links and reload initialize their requested section
The latest click wins when an earlier section response is delayed
A failed section fetch offers an in-page retry without replacing the document
Old independent URLs remain directly usable and keep their canonical URLs
Navigating from an old game moves its live DOM, progress and audio into home
Project-prefix deployment resolves imported links, responsive pictures and media
A legacy subpath entry can open the home gallery with correctly rebased pictures
A rejected feature script retries in place, including the native module cache
The shared content helper is lazy, retries a failed load and is reused
A high-density phone defers the larger about avatar until needed
Native smooth scroll settles below the header and the final music section stays active
Normal section navigation has no missing resources or console exceptions
expectedFailures: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 503 (Service Unavailable)

notes: A full 17-suite pass preceded the final cover attribute-order fix; unit, sections, source-sections, music, music-gesture and compat were rerun afterwards. WebKit section tests also passed after the fix.
Initial WebKit avatar request assertion caught a transient oversized music cover request; sizes is now assigned before srcset.
Transfer size includes HTTP headers and all requests observed during Lighthouse load, including speculative lazy images.
Load-time differences are small and do not establish a stable speed improvement; byte reduction is consistent across all runs.
